description:
if an aim had a status change, it should be possible to show a status change history and for each status change commit the diff of the entire repo (code) of that commit. Since aim status changes are committed along with code changes. 
Ui wise... make a "show history" button next to the status select box in the edit aim modal. 
And then bring up a diff modal... 
The diff modal shows on the top a row of status changes: 
<status A (unclickable)> date of commit (clickable) <status B (unclickable)> date of commit (clickable) <status C (unclickable)>
line breaks if too long. 

then, below, on the left side a tree of changed files. 
and on the right side the diff of the selected file. 

maybe there is already an npm/vite plugin for git diff visualization? 
then consider using this for conformity

status.comment: Implemented and checked in the live UI (localhost:4000). A 'history' button next to the status select opens status chips (project status colors) joined by clickable commit dates; the latest change is preselected. Below: a tree of the commit's changed files (code first) and a colored unified diff. Escape closes only the history and returns focus to the button. Plain unified diff, no diff library. Awaiting Felix's acceptance.

reflection: Live check on two aims (open→human-dependent; open→cancelled→open→done): chips and dates rendered, the diff loaded, no outer scrollbar after removing a flex:1 that overrode the diff area's height, and Escape/Escape closed history then the edit modal. Found and fixed during the check: grey chips for statuses without CSS variables (now project status colors), the outer scrollbar, and lost focus after closing (Escape no longer reached the edit modal). An apparent Escape failure mid-session was a hot-reload artifact and did not reproduce after a page reload. Backend tested against a temp git repo (4/4 git-evidence tests).
